title: Can a sort never compare two items?
hook: Sort ten scores by dropping them in buckets. Does anything need to be bigger?

knows: a whole number can label a position
doesNotKnow: that sorting can use no comparisons when values are small whole numbers

misconception: Sorting always works by comparing items to each other.
objective: The learner can say that counting sort tallies each value into a bucket and reads the buckets in order, so it needs no comparisons, but only works when values are whole numbers in a small known range.

claims.text: Tallying the scores 3 0 5 2 2 1 4 5 0 3 gives 2, 1, 2, 2, 1, 2 for scores 0 to 5, and reading the buckets in order gives 0 0 1 2 2 3 3 4 5 5.
claims.source: Node script: tallies of [3,0,5,2,2,1,4,5,0,3] = [2,1,2,2,1,2]; read out = 0 0 1 2 2 3 3 4 5 5. Demo.tsx derives both from the same SCORES array.

claims.text: Sorting by tallying and writing out takes 0 comparisons between scores: each score goes to the bucket with its own number.
claims.source: The procedure only increments a tally indexed by the score and writes values out in index order; no step tests one score against another. CLRS 3rd ed. section 8.2 (COUNTING-SORT uses array indexing, not comparisons of keys with each other).

claims.text: This works because the scores are whole numbers in a small range, 0 to 5.
claims.source: CLRS 8.2: COUNTING-SORT assumes each of n inputs is an integer in the range 0 to k.

claims.text: With a huge range of possible values you would need a bucket for every possible value.
claims.source: CLRS 8.2: it uses an array of k+1 counters, so memory and time include a term in k (running time Theta(n + k)).

claims.text: The question: ten scores, each a whole number from 0 to 5, sorted by tallying; answer 0 comparisons (2 and 3 above). Distractors 9 and 33 are plain numbers, not claims.
claims.source: Builder scope note: options are distractors only; the reveal does not explain them.

recall.question: Seven ages, each a whole number from 0 to 9, are sorted by tallying how many of each age occur and writing them out. How many comparisons between ages does that take?
recall.why: Each age goes to the bucket with its own number, and the buckets are read in order, so no age is compared with another. It works because the range 0 to 9 is small.
